title: Kenny Smith Raises 20% of Lasry Group's Las Vegas NBA Bid
htmlContent:
The race to own the NBA's first Las Vegas franchise is entering its final stretch, and one of the contenders just got a lot more interesting. According to Chris Haynes, Senior NBA Insider for NBA on Prime and The Association on NBA TV, the ownership group led by Canadian billionaire Steve Apostolopoulos and former Milwaukee Bucks co-owner Marc Lasry remains very much in play for the expansion team. Haynes added a notable detail: Kenny Smith, the two-time NBA champion and longtime fixture of "Inside the NBA," is part of the group and has raised 20 percent of the bid.

Sources: Ownership group of Marc Lasry (former Bucks co-owner) & Canadian billionaire Steve Apostolopoulos remain in play for Las Vegas NBA Expansion bid. I’m also told Kenny Smith from “Inside The NBA” is part of the ownership group and has raised 20 percent of the bid. https://t.co/7fLkwbycon

— Chris Haynes (@ChrisBHaynes) October 23, 2026

That last point changes how the bid should be viewed. Smith is not simply lending his name and television profile to a group of financiers. If Haynes' sourcing holds, he has helped assemble a meaningful share of the capital in a process expected to cost well into the billions.

A Finalist Group Still Standing

The league has narrowed the Las Vegas field to three finalists: Nancy Walton Laurie and Bill Laurie; Steve Apostolopoulos and Marc Lasry; and Vegas Golden Knights owner Bill Foley alongside Hall of Famer Jerry Colangelo. Reporting from ESPN earlier in the process put the price for the franchise and a new arena at roughly $12 billion to $13 billion, with the league expected to pick a winner soon and complete the formal approval process before the end of the year.

Haynes' report signals that the Apostolopoulos-Lasry group has not slipped behind as that decision approaches. In a contest with this much money involved, staying in contention this late is a statement on its own.

The Men at the Top

Apostolopoulos, who leads the group with his brothers Jim and Peter, is the founder of private equity firm Six Ventures and runs the real estate company Triple Group of Companies. He has chased major sports properties before, holding talks to buy the Charlotte Hornets from Michael Jordan in 2023 and pursuing both the NFL's Washington Commanders and the NHL's Ottawa Senators. Those efforts fell short, but they made clear he wants a place among North America's major-league owners.

Lasry brings the experience the league values most: he has done this before. He bought into the Bucks in 2014 for $550 million, served as the team's governor during Milwaukee's 2021 championship run, and sold his stake in 2023. He now chairs Avenue Capital, which recently closed a sports-focused fund with more than $1 billion in commitments. For the NBA's Board of Governors, a familiar face who has already navigated league ownership is a valuable asset.

Kenny Smith's Bigger Role

Smith's involvement had already been floated publicly when ESPN's Stephen A. Smith used an appearance on "First Take" to say he was rooting for "The Jet" and his group to land Las Vegas. Haynes' reporting now ties Smith to a specific finalist and gives a sense of his weight inside it.

Raising 20 percent of a bid of this size would make Smith one of the most financially involved former players in any recent ownership pursuit. It also gives the group something rivals may struggle to match: a recognizable basketball voice with decades of relationships across the league, its players and its media partners. Celebrity investors are common in team purchases, but a former player responsible for a fifth of the money is not.

The Competition

None of this makes the Apostolopoulos-Lasry group the favorite. The Lauries pair Walmart-family wealth with prior ownership of the NHL's St. Louis Blues and a home in nearby Henderson. Foley and Colangelo combine deep local ties, Foley's success with the Golden Knights and Colangelo's long-standing league relationships, and their group has its own basketball names in Vinny Del Negro and Jay Williams. They have also said they would build a new arena if selected.

What Comes Next

The NBA has targeted as early as the 2028–29 season for its Las Vegas and Seattle expansion teams to begin play. Reports have also indicated that the Las Vegas runners-up could shift their attention to the Seattle process, meaning the groups that miss out in the desert may not be done.

For now, Haynes' reporting makes clear that the Apostolopoulos-Lasry bid is still a live option, and that Kenny Smith may be closer than ever to trading a seat on the studio desk for a seat in an owner's suite.
excerpt: According to NBA Insider Chris Haynes, Kenny Smith — the two-time champion and longtime "Inside the NBA" fixture — has raised 20 percent of the Apostolopoulos-Lasry group's bid for the NBA's first Las Vegas expansion franchise, making him one of the most financially involved former players in any recent ownership pursuit.
